newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE DAMS DRYING UP DUE TO EL NINO.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE DAMS DRYING UP DUE TO EL NINO.

text.p: Water levels in five major dams in the Philippines have dipped below normal levels due to below-average rainfall in recent weeks, experts at the Philippine weather bureau said on Friday.

Hydrologist Roy Badilla of the Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration said Lake Lanao, the principal source of water supply in southern Mindanao island, is experiencing low water inflows.
Lake Lanao is also used as a reservoir by hydroelectric power plants in Mindanao, which account for 90 percent of the island's power needs.

Badilla told reporters the water level in Pantabangan dam in Nueva Ecija province in central Luzon, the country's rice bowl, had dropped to 181.7 meters above sea level, or 39.3 meters below the desired level.
Water level in Angat dam in Bulacan province, also in central Luzon, had dropped to 185.58 meters from its normal level of 212.
"Angat dam is drying up. Normally, when there is rain, the water level reaches up to the spill way," Badilla said.
Badilla said water levels in the Binga, Magat and Ambuklao dams are also experiencing weak water inflows.
The Philippines is now supposed to be at the height of its rainy season, which normally starts April and ends in September.
But weather experts said most parts of the country experienced sparse rains between April and July this year due to fewer-than-usual cyclones.
They attributed this to El Nino, a weather condition caused by warming of water in the western Pacific ocean which creates drought in some areas and heavier-than-normal rainfall in others.
